journey.text: Bootcamps built capability. Hackathons tested it. Each milestone moved Janakpur’s technology community forward in a different way.

items.title: The first full-stack cohort
items.story: We opened our first focused learning room around React, Django and the habits of practical software development.
items.result: Students moved beyond college theory and began building, versioning and presenting working web applications.

items.title: Janakpur builds under pressure
items.story: The city’s first community hackathon brought teams together to move from problem statements to working prototypes.
items.result: Local builders could collaborate, make technical decisions quickly and present their ideas to a judging panel.

items.title: A deeper move into data and AI
items.story: The second cohort expanded the program into Python, machine learning and intelligent systems through project-led sessions.
items.result: Learners gained a practical path into AI by working with datasets, models and real application ideas—not theory alone.

items.title: The community returned to ship again
items.story: A second rapid-build sprint gave new teams the same intense cycle of ideation, coding, feedback and final demos.
items.result: The first event was not a one-off. Janakpur now had a repeatable stage for teamwork, competition and youth innovation.

items.title: A regional conversation about AI
items.story: We brought speakers, students and technology enthusiasts into one room for ideas, questions and community connection.
items.result: The community gained direct access to industry perspectives and a larger vision for technology leadership in Madhesh.

items.title: Full-stack engineering meets AI
items.story: The new program joins modern frontend, dependable backend architecture and practical AI APIs in one sequential path.
items.result: Ten-plus GitHub projects and a deployed full-stack AI capstone built for a live portfolio and Demo Day.

faq.text: Everything students and parents ask before joining a new cohort.

items.question: What if I do not know programming yet?
items.answer: You can still prepare. Before the screening, learn variables, conditions, loops and functions in C, C++ or Java, plus basic HTML and CSS. Dedication and basic logical thinking matter more than already knowing every tool.

items.question: How does the screening interview work?
items.answer: It is a friendly 10-minute conversation about basic logic, your motivation, laptop readiness and whether you can commit to the daily learning schedule.

items.question: How do I register?
items.answer: Registration, reminders, interview updates and calendar details are handled in one reliable place. You will leave this website to complete your application securely there.

items.question: Do I need a high-end laptop?
items.answer: No. A standard working Windows, Mac or Linux laptop with 8GB RAM is enough for VS Code, Python, Vite, Django and SQLite.

items.question: What happens around public holidays?
items.answer: The program includes a built-in 10-day flex buffer for public holidays, catch-up labs and project sprints, so the core curriculum does not need to be rushed.

finalCta.text: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Start with a short registration, then meet us for a friendly screening conversation.
